quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: If you must stop quickly in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Brake hard on both brakes while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly in a curve, first straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten out, apply the brakes slowly and smoothly while reducing your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags. Placing loads high on a sissy bar or frame is dangerous because it raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert riders about upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: Riders rarely hear a tire going flat. You will notice tire problems by changes in how the motorcycle handles instead.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
You may block another vehicle from passing.
The near side of the lane is better.
You will feel more wind blast on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Stay near the passing vehicle when being passed. Moving to the far side of the lane may encourage the driver to return to your lane before they have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles handle differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve exactly. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: Studies show that most crash-involved riders:

options.text: Use the front brake too little and the rear brake too much.
Use the front brake too much and the rear brake too little.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front brake too little and the rear brake too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders involved in crashes use the front brake too little and the rear brake too much.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done to avoid a hazard on a slippery road.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick maneuver that needs a lot of traction. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are usually rectangular and white with black lettering or symbols. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When someone passes you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay in the right part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: You need more following distance when stopping takes longer, the pavement is slippery, you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy. If you can see through the vehicle in front, you do not need extra distance.

questions.question: When riding in a traffic lane, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on how road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust:
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks because of this extra weight. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors since the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders behind them can watch and help if needed.

questions.question: What can increase fatigue while riding?

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from tiring weather like wind and rain. Limit rides to six hours per day and take a break every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue can happen when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding at night, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: Darkness makes it harder to see and judge distance. Use at least three seconds of following distance at night. You need extra time to realize a vehicle has stopped and to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you usually do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a wet lane is especially dangerous. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: If you must brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than on a straight road.
Brake as hard as on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when the motorcycle is leaning. Try to straighten up before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes smoothly and gently.

questions.question: How do you get the strongest braking in a straight line?

options.text: Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.explanation: The strongest braking happens when you apply both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do when turning left on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean the right way, press the handgrip in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: A dog is chasing your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the animal to lose interest.
Slow down as you approach the animal, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the animal, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, downshift and slow down as you approach it. Then accelerate and ride away from it.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space so drivers can see the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching the curb.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should the rider do?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the motorcycle and turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. But in slow, tight turns, keep your body upright to balance the leaning motorcycle.
